correctness.rationale: Complete proof: Govc freeness forces all two-primary torsion to be detected by a mod-two rank loss in the top boundary. The 24-by-24 deletion matrix has nine-dimensional binary kernel and exactly 369 nonzero vectors of weight at most 12. Exact rational ranks identify precisely 52 independent supports, all weight 12, and the linear-matroid circuit argument proves global minimality. Relabeling/reversal partitions the 52 into five orbits (2,6,8,12,24); exact unimodular Smith reductions on representatives give eleven unit factors and one factor two. All cases have the full simply-connected two-skeleton with H2 rank 15, so Smith reductions of attaching maps give the claimed Moore space plus three two-spheres. Standalone checker and recorded output were replayed; proof does not extrapolate from small experimental cases.

A broad indexed published-finding corpus search and primary full-text comparisons found no covering theorem; priority is best-knowledge, not absolute uniqueness.

value.rationale: The problem asks how economically higher torsion can be realized in the first alphabet where it is possible for permutation complexes. Prior sources gave 15 and 12 explicit upper bounds but no optimality proof. The exact twelve-facet threshold, all 52 labeled minimizers, five combinatorial symmetry types and common Moore-space homotopy type solve a natural finite minimal-complexity classification rather than a randomly chosen invariant. The binary matroid-circuit technique also gives a reproducible way to approach larger alphabets.
